name: Lori Stacy
current_role: Chair of the Board, Trader Interactive (retired as CEO Dec 2023)
profile: Lori Stacy is the long-time leader of Trader Interactive (Norfolk, VA), the marketplace business behind vertical listing sites such as RV Trader, Cycle Trader and Equipment Trader. She joined Auto Trader in 1997 as a sales manager, became CEO in 2017, steered the company through its 2021-22 sale to Australia's carsales.com, and retired as CEO in Dec 2023, staying on as board chair.
interesting_fact: carsales.com bought 49% of Trader Interactive in 2021 and agreed to buy the remaining 51% in 2022; carsales CEO Cameron McIntyre said 'Lori is a strong, capable leader who built a world-class business'.
deep_cut_fact: She started at Auto Trader in 1997 as a sales manager and rose through the ranks by building up the non-automotive brands (RVs, motorcycles, equipment) before taking the CEO job in 2017 -- a 25-year career at one company.
notes: Hurun lists her as 'founder' but she was a career executive/CEO, not a founder (Trader Interactive spun out of Dominion Enterprises). Company site blocks bots; no published press email found. Best route: Trader Interactive corporate communications.

name: Philippe Corrot
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Mirakl (Paris/Boston); co-CEO Steve Tzikakis reports to him since Nov 2026
profile: Paris-born serial e-commerce founder (b. 1976). With Adrien Nussenbaum he built SplitGames, sold it to Fnac in 2008, ran Fnac's marketplace, then founded Mirakl in 2012 -- the marketplace software used by Macy's, Kroger, Carrefour, H&M and others. Mirakl became a unicorn in 2020, turned profitable in 2025 and is pushing 'agentic commerce' (Mirakl Nexus).
interesting_fact: He co-wrote 'The Online Marketplace Advantage' (Wiley, 2023) with Adrien Nussenbaum, which became a Wall Street Journal bestseller; he calls AI a 'change of civilisation' for business.
deep_cut_fact: Before Mirakl, he and Nussenbaum ran SplitGames (founded 2006), an online marketplace for trading used video games; Fnac bought it in 2008 and the pair spent three years building Fnac's own marketplace -- the experience that became Mirakl's playbook. He reportedly taught himself to code at age 4.
notes: Nov 10 2026 governance change: ex-Sitecore CEO Steve Tzikakis joined as co-CEO reporting to Corrot; co-founder Adrien Nussenbaum became chairman. Corrot keeps strategy, product, tech; good podcast angle on AI agents in commerce.

name: Shen Ronghua
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of GalaxySpace (银河航天), the Beijing satellite-internet/LEO constellation company. Public sources name Xu Ming (ex-Cheetah Mobile co-founder/CTO) as GalaxySpace's founder, chairman and CEO, with Gao Qianfeng and Liu Chang as co-founders; no public record links a 'Shen Ronghua' to the company.
notes: Identity could not be confirmed -- possibly a Hurun romanisation error or a minor shareholder. GalaxySpace founder is Xu Ming (徐鸣); the company filed for A-share IPO tutoring in March 2026 (https://www.cls.cn/detail/2330307). Verify Chinese name before any outreach.

name: Harsimarbir Singh
current_role: Co-founder, Pristyn Care (leads business, technology and growth)
profile: Harsimarbir 'Harsh' Singh co-founded Pristyn Care in 2018 with Dr. Garima Sawhney and Dr. Vaibhav Kapoor. The Gurugram-based company runs an end-to-end care-delivery model for elective surgeries across Indian cities, partnering with hospitals and its own surgeons; it became a unicorn in Dec 2021 with backing from Tiger Global, Sequoia and Hummingbird.
interesting_fact: Pristyn Care was his fourth startup: he says he failed three times over about ten years before it worked, and after the third shutdown 'wanted to do anything but start up again'.
deep_cut_fact: His earlier ventures included an electricity-theft detection business (~2010), a Groupon-style restaurant app and a hyperlocal quick-commerce delivery service (~2015); between failures he worked at Urban Company in its pre-revenue days. His line: 'There's always noise in failure; it's the success that gives you clarity.'
notes: Low public profile; best covered via Entrepreneur India and Hummingbird features. No published press email found on Pristyn Care site.

name: Pierre-Baptiste Béchu
current_role: Co-founder, Aircall; leads the communications-platform (VoIP/WebRTC) engineering team
profile: French engineer and one of Aircall's four co-founders (with Olivier Pailhès, Xavier Durand and Jonathan Anguelov). Joining in 2014, he built the first version of Aircall's backend and infrastructure; the cloud phone system for sales and support teams reached a $1B+ valuation in 2021. He now runs the engineering team behind Aircall's global voice platform and has served as interim CTPO.
interesting_fact: Unusual dual training: a Master of Engineering from École Centrale de Lyon plus a master's in industrial and organizational psychology from Université Lumière Lyon 2.
deep_cut_fact: He personally wrote the first version of Aircall's backend and infrastructure in 2014, and today leads 20+ engineers keeping its worldwide voice services reliable -- voice quality and security are his core focus.
notes: Technical, low-profile co-founder (no CEO role); Aircall's press room lists no email. Also an angel investor (50 Partners, per aggregator profiles -- unverified). A data/infra-focused podcast angle fits him.

name: Michael McDerment
current_role: Co-founder and Chair of the Board, FreshBooks (Toronto); CEO 2003-2021
profile: Mike McDerment co-founded FreshBooks in Toronto with Levi Cooperman and Joe Sawada, growing it from a web-design shop's invoicing tool into cloud accounting software for small businesses worldwide. He bootstrapped for about a decade before raising $30M (2014) and later reaching a $1B+ valuation; he handed the CEO role to Don Epperson in 2021 and remains board chair.
interesting_fact: FreshBooks began in 2003 when he accidentally saved over an old invoice while billing clients of his small web-design agency; frustrated, he built his own billing tool and ran the business from his parents' basement for about 3.5 years.
deep_cut_fact: His first businesses straight out of college were an Ultimate Frisbee tournament and a league; a caterer for the event needed a website, which is how he drifted into web design -- the agency that later spawned FreshBooks.
notes: Press contact is Chloe Matcham, Senior Manager, Communications (named on FreshBooks press releases). FreshBooks recently launched an Anthropic MCP connector -- AI/small-business angle. CEO seat has turned over several times since 2021; McDerment's own status beyond 'chair' not confirmed for 2026.

name: Eynat Guez
profile: French-born Israeli entrepreneur (raised in Netanya) who co-founded Papaya Global in 2016 with Ofer Herman and Ruben Drong. The payroll and workforce-payments platform hit a $3.7B valuation in 2021, making it Israel's first woman-led unicorn; it now processes tens of billions in annual payments and is pushing agentic-AI compliance products (Papaya One, Papaya Talent in 2026).
interesting_fact: Papaya is her third company: she earlier founded Relocation Source (2009, corporate relocation) and Expert Source (helping firms expand into East Asia), after seven years as COO of LR Group, a holding company running infrastructure projects in Africa.
deep_cut_fact: Before business she worked as a youth journalist (Channel 2, Israeli Educational TV, Ma'ariv La'noar), served in the IDF as an F-16 squadron adjutant, and was a competitive swimmer; she sits on the board of Hagal Shely, an NGO that uses the sea (surfing) as therapy.
notes: Media-friendly CEO; frequent podcast guest (e.g. Fintech Leaders). Press contact on 2026 releases is Naomi Fletcher. Reports (Finance Magnates) say Papaya has explored a sale at up to $4.5B.

name: Naysawn Naji
current_role: Co-founder and former CPO of Wrapbook (left 2022); reportedly founded Buildpal, a scheduling tool for general contractors
profile: Product-focused fintech founder who co-founded Wrapbook in 2018 with Hesham El-Nahhas, Ali Javid (CEO) and Cameron Woodward. Wrapbook, a payroll and onboarding platform for film/TV/commercial productions, raised a $100M Series B at a $1B valuation in 2021 (Tiger Global, a16z). Naji left in 2022 and moved on to construction software (Buildpal).
interesting_fact: The Wrapbook idea started at a New York tech open-mic, where an actor demoed an app she had built to help actors book gigs; he was unimpressed until he learned it had 4,000 paying users, convincing him media production was ripe for better software.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wrapbook he was co-founder and CPO of Arcus, a Latin America-focused bill-payment API, where he and future co-founder Hesham El-Nahhas had lunch together 'every day for four years'; one early Wrapbook check came blind from a friend of his at Google.
notes: Low public profile; no published contact found. Buildpal role comes from Contrary Research (2024) and could not be independently confirmed. Wrapbook's later 2024 round was at $750M.

name: Thomas Zhu
current_role: Co-founder (and formerly CTO), Amber Group; current role at listed successor Amber International (Nasdaq: AMBR) not confirmed
profile: Software engineer and the sixth co-founder of Amber Group, the Hong Kong/Singapore crypto trading and wealth-management firm started by ex-Morgan Stanley traders. While a Bloomberg developer exploring machine learning for trading, he joined their 2015 side project; Amber went full-time into crypto in 2017 and reached a $1B+ valuation in 2021 and ~$3B in 2022.
interesting_fact: Unlike his five co-founders, who sat together on Morgan Stanley's Hong Kong fixed-income trading floor, Zhu was the outsider: a Bloomberg developer working on machine learning for trading.
deep_cut_fact: Amber began in 2015 -- with the founders all in their 20s -- as a side project running algorithmic trading on Chinese stocks and index futures, before pivoting full-time to crypto arbitrage.
notes: Very low public profile. Not named in 2025-26 Amber International (AMBR) filings/releases; Michael Wu is chairman/CEO. Contacts are company-level only.

name: Wayne Lin
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Upside (Washington, DC); COO 2016-2023
profile: Wayne Lin co-founded Upside (formerly GetUpside) with CEO Alex Kinnier and others after both were product executives at Opower, the utility-energy-savings software firm that IPO'd in 2014 and was bought by Oracle. Upside's app gives consumers personalized cash back at gas stations, grocers and restaurants, paid from merchants' incremental profit; it reached a $1B+ valuation in 2021. Earlier he was a Google product manager on ad tech.
interesting_fact: Upside's model is pay-for-performance: 'Only when they make more profit than they made today do we make money,' Lin said in 2017, when the app was live at 650 D.C.-area gas stations and had paid out $300K in cash back. Google chief economist Hal Varian advised the startup.
deep_cut_fact: The Upside idea came from his Opower years, watching how consumers responded to personalized nudges to save on utility bills; the 2017 app even had a #GasForGood option letting users donate cash back to local charities like the Capital Area Food Bank.
notes: Energy angle: ex-Opower product/analytics VP. Don't confuse with a different Wayne Lin (Berkeley/Amazon, Mooncat/Nostos Health). No published press email on Upside newsroom.

name: Michael Fey
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Island (Dallas-based enterprise browser company)
profile: Veteran security executive -- ex-President/COO of Symantec and Blue Coat, CTO of Intel Security and EVP of enterprise products at McAfee, and briefly CEO of D2iQ -- who co-founded Island with CTO Dan Amiga in 2020. Island builds a security-first enterprise browser and now pitches it as the control plane for AI agents; it raised a $400M Series F at a $6.4B valuation in Oct 2026.
interesting_fact: Island was born from an acquisition: Fey met co-founder Dan Amiga when Symantec bought Amiga's browser-isolation startup Fireglass in 2017; after leaving Symantec in 2018 Fey planned to move into private equity before the two decided to rebuild the browser itself.
deep_cut_fact: He studied Engineering Physics and Mathematics at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University, co-authored the book 'Security Battleground: An Executive Field Manual', and deliberately built Island in Dallas rather than Silicon Valley.

public_contacts.value: Andy Shane, Big Valley Marketing for Island - ashane@bigvalley.co

notes: Frequent conference speaker (RSA, Black Hat) and podcast guest; open to media. Strong AI-agents/enterprise-infrastructure angle. Series F source: https://newshub.medianet.com.au/2026/10/islandannounces-400-million-series-f-bringing-valuation-to-6-4-billion/175049/

name: Abhishek Agrawal
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Material Security (CEO since April 2023; previously CTO)
profile: Princeton electrical engineer and Harvard MBA who was an early product leader at Dropbox and an engineer at Microsoft Research. In 2017 he co-founded Material Security with ex-Dropbox colleagues Ryan Noon and Chris Park to protect Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 email, files and accounts; the company passed a $1B valuation (Andreessen Horowitz, Elad Gil backers).
interesting_fact: Material was inspired by the 2016 US election email hacks -- notably the breach of Clinton campaign chair John Podesta's Gmail -- and the idea that attackers will win round one, so the job is to make the 'second round' (what they can do with a compromised mailbox) much harder.
deep_cut_fact: Before settling on email security, he and his co-founders reportedly listed about 25 startup ideas, narrowed them to four and tried selling each before committing. At Dropbox he shipped collaboration products as well as core infrastructure and analytics.
notes: Podcast-friendly (has appeared on The Desi VC, Duo Decipher). The '25 ideas' detail is from a podcast summary and is less firmly sourced. No published press email on the Material site.

name: Aza Steel
current_role: Co-founder, GoGuardian (Los Angeles edtech); current position not publicly confirmed
profile: UCLA sociology graduate who taught himself to code and founded GoGuardian in 2014 with fellow Bruin Advait Shinde (later CEO). GoGuardian grew from a Chrome-extension laptop tracker into classroom-management and student-safety software used by thousands of US schools; it reached a $1B+ valuation and took investment from Thoma Bravo in 2021.
interesting_fact: GoGuardian began as his dorm-room Chrome extension to track his own laptop if it was stolen -- a 'flawed plan' since it relied on the thief using Chrome -- until school districts flooded him with requests to use it.
deep_cut_fact: When GoGuardian scaled so fast its servers were 'literally melting', he called AWS support daily as 'an emotional and technological crutch' and kept getting Australian agents: 'that accent was just really soothing.' He and Shinde made Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2016.
notes: Very low public profile since ~2018; no current role or published contact found. Name sometimes misspelled 'Steele'. Best route may be via GoGuardian corporate communications.

name: Christian Floerkemeier
current_role: Co-founder, CTO and VP Product, Scandit (Zurich)
profile: Cambridge-trained electrical engineer with an ETH Zurich computer-science PhD who was Associate Director of MIT's Auto-ID Lab, part of the team behind RFID tech now used in major supply chains. In 2009 he co-founded Scandit with fellow ETH PhDs Samuel Mueller and Christof Roduner; its smartphone computer-vision barcode/'smart data capture' software made it a $1B unicorn in 2022.
interesting_fact: Scandit was bootstrapped for three and a half years, only raising its first round in 2013; he did all the early product, algorithm and computer-vision work himself and jokes that he once did the jobs of everyone who now reports to him.
deep_cut_fact: Within his first week as a PhD student he joined a Walmart-MIT research collaboration on the 'next-generation barcode'; he also co-founded Fosstrak, the leading open-source RFID software platform.
notes: Technical co-founder, comfortable with media (writes bylines, speaks at NRF). Fosstrak detail confirmed on Scandit management page.
